chapter: Shows, scripts and the Mosby-era names
title: Writing film shorts for the would-be producer
summary: Spikes wrote several short screenplays with shooting notes for a producer who never made them, planning even a life of Lionel Hampton.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: So, then, but you switched from stage to screen playwriting, right?

Well, I...as I told you, this white fella come up there, and he started to hangin' 'round there because he'd been...his place had been closed, and he had no place to hang out or nothin', and he come down, and he used to hang around there, and...and he had a cameraman that he knew and everything, and we got to talkin' and was gonna make shorts-- you know, one-reel shorts and things. So I wrote several little things-- "Harlemesque" and...oh...somethin' 'bout a guy...I wrote one there where a fellow was...he and his partner--one was a smart guy and the other was a kind of a lackey, and he...he was going to go into the motion pic...uh, go into the production business, and he was gonna...finally sit down and some talk how they could raise the money and everything, you know. And they was going to put on the show, and he sold the idea to some poor workin' man ...took all his money...[chuckles]...oh, it was funny, and the shows come in there and he never did get into production. I don't...I had it around here somewhere. I don't know. And I wrote two, three of them little things. Had 'em all in books with the shooting and ever'thing. He took...set down and done all this--how we shoot this and close and up and the way and distance and everything, but...and he had a...was gonna make the life of Lionel. Here, see. And finally, he got a few dollars, and I never seen him no more.
